skill.name: extract-from-pdfs
skill.description: Extract structured data from scientific PDFs for systematic reviews, research databases, and meta-analyses using schema-driven Claude workflows.
skill.summary: Turn scientific PDF collections into validated datasets for analysis.
skill.author: brunoasm

security_audit.summary: The scripts use file writes, API calls, and environment variables for the declared PDF extraction workflow. The audit confirms the curl-to-shell installer guidance, shell-profile API key persistence, and plaintext HTTP validation calls as security issues. Most backtick, key-name, ID, SQLite, and output-write alerts are benign examples or normal user-directed operations; no prompt injection text was found.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to a shell.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the curl-to-shell instruction with package manager installation, manual download, and checksum verification steps.

remediation.issue: Setup guide recommends storing an API key in a shell profile.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the echo-to-bashrc guidance. Recommend session-only variables, ignored local env files, or a secret manager.

remediation.issue: Some validation calls use plaintext HTTP.
remediation.suggestion: Use HTTPS endpoints where available, or document the privacy risk and disable those validators by default.

remediation.issue: External validation sends extracted values to third-party services.
remediation.suggestion: Document each external API destination and recommend skip-validation for confidential datasets.

content.value_statement: Researchers often need repeatable data extraction from many scientific PDFs, but manual review is slow and hard to validate. This skill guides a schema-driven pipeline that filters papers, extracts structured records with Claude, validates results, and exports analysis files.
actual_capabilities: Organizes PDF metadata from BibTeX, RIS, DOI lists, or directories.
Filters papers by abstract with Claude Haiku, Claude Sonnet, or local Ollama models.
Extracts schema-defined structured records from PDFs using Claude vision.
Repairs and validates extraction JSON against a schema.
Enriches selected fields with GBIF, WFO, GeoNames, PubChem, NCBI, or geocoding APIs.
Prepares validation sets and calculates precision, recall, and F1 metrics.
limitations: Requires local Python dependencies and API credentials for Claude-based extraction.
Extraction quality depends on PDF quality, schema design, and model behavior.
External validation APIs may receive extracted field values unless validation is skipped.
Very large or protected PDFs may exceed provider size limits or fail processing.

use_cases.title: Run Systematic Reviews
use_cases.description: Convert a paper collection into structured extraction results for review, screening, and synthesis.

use_cases.title: Build Research Databases
use_cases.description: Create analysis-ready datasets from published PDFs with validation and export steps.

use_cases.title: Measure Extraction Quality
use_cases.description: Prepare annotation samples and compare automated extraction against ground truth metrics.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Project
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new PDF collection.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use extract-from-pdfs to plan a workflow for 60 papers. Ask me for the required inputs, then propose the first commands and files.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Schema
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design an extraction schema for clinical trial PDFs. Include fields for population, intervention, comparison, outcome, sample size, and notes.

prompt_templates.title: Run Extraction and Validation
prompt_templates.scenario: Execute the main workflow after setup.
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through filtering abstracts, extracting from selected PDFs, repairing outputs, validating fields with APIs, and exporting CSV and SQLite results.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Model Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare two extraction runs from different models. Prepare a validation sample, calculate precision, recall, and F1, then summarize weak fields.

output_examples.input: A Zotero BibTeX export, a PDF folder, and a schema for ecology interaction records.
output: Standardized paper metadata with PDF paths.
A filtered list of papers likely to contain relevant records.
Cleaned extraction results ready for validation and export.

output_examples.input: Filtered papers and cleaned extraction results that need quality review.
output_examples.output: A validation sample with selected papers, plus metrics for precision, recall, F1, and weak fields.

output_examples.input: Validated extraction results for a meta-analysis dataset.
output_examples.output: Analysis-ready exports for spreadsheet review, Python workflows, R workflows, or SQLite queries.

best_practices: Start with a small test set before running the full corpus.
Review schema fields with domain experts before extraction.
Keep API keys out of shared shell profiles and repository files.
anti_patterns: Do not process confidential PDFs through external APIs without approval.
Do not treat model output as final data without validation.
Do not change prompts after the full run without documenting the change.

faq.question: Do I need an API key?
faq.answer: Yes for Claude filtering or PDF extraction. Local Ollama filtering can run without an Anthropic key.

faq.question: Can this run only on my machine?
faq.answer: Abstract filtering can use Ollama locally. Full PDF extraction uses Claude unless you customize the scripts.

faq.question: Which input sources are supported?
faq.answer: The workflow supports BibTeX, RIS, DOI lists, and directories of PDF files.

faq.question: Can it validate extracted values?
faq.answer: Yes. It can validate selected fields with scientific APIs such as GBIF, WFO, GeoNames, PubChem, and NCBI.

faq.question: How is extraction quality measured?
faq.answer: The validation workflow compares automated extraction with annotated ground truth and reports precision, recall, and F1.

faq.question: Is it suitable for sensitive documents?
faq.answer: Use caution. Skip external validation and review provider policies before sending sensitive PDFs or fields to APIs.
